text: Green roofs and cool roofs – known collectively as 'eco-roofs' – help make Toronto more resilient and better adapted to climate change. Eco-roofs reduce urban heat and its associated energy use. Green roofs also help manage storm water runoff, enhance biodiversity, improve air quality, and beautify our city. In 2008, Toronto established the Eco-Roof Incentive Program to encourage the installation of eco-roofs on existing buildings and some new buildings. In 2013, the program became completely self-sustaining by drawing funding from cash-in-lieu payments through the Green Roof Bylaw. In December 2016, a new reporting requirement was adopted by City Council, stating that a staff report be submitted with a recommendation to the Planning and Growth Management Committee and City Council for applications for project funding greater than $50,000 for cool roofs and greater than $100,000 for…

City Council on March 26 and 27, 2018, adopted the following: 1. City Council approve Eco-Roof Incentive Program funding for a cool roof at 1460 Wickman Road of 29,339 square metres, in an amount up to $96,695 above the pre-approved funding of $50,000.
